title: The month-end close rollout
scenario:
You lead finance operations at a manufacturer. 60 accountants build the month-end reporting package. The CFO wants an AI assistant to draft the package, and asks for a company-wide launch next Monday.

You ran an 8-person pilot for two closes. The exhibit shows the CFO's launch plan and your pilot numbers.
exhibit:
CFO launch plan (made-up example data)
  Monday: all 60 accountants get access
  Support: one 30-minute webinar, no named contact
  Measurement: none planned
  Review: "we will see how it goes"

Pilot: 8 accountants, 2 closes, same 8 people vs their previous 2 closes
                                  Before      Pilot
  Days to finish the draft         6.0         4.5
  Corrections found at review      9           15

Heard in the pilot
  Senior accountant: "I tried it once and it got a number wrong. I don't
  trust it with the package."

questions.prompt: What is the best change to the CFO's launch plan?

options.text: Replace the big launch with staged steps from the pilot, with a baseline, a contact and a dated review.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's controlled rollout selects a limited group and a workflow, compares with a baseline and reviews outcomes before expanding.

options.text: Launch on Monday as planned, but also send a longer email about the new tool and how to use it to all staff.
options.explanation: More announcement doesn't add a baseline, a contact or a review. The Claude Code champion kit says adoption rarely follows an announcement.

options.text: Start over with a new pilot that includes all 60 accountants, because 8 people are too few to learn from.
options.explanation: The pilot already gave useful numbers. A small, controlled group is how the OpenAI guide starts a rollout.

options.text: Launch to all 60 and let each person decide for themselves whether they want to use the tool at all.
options.explanation: That skips the baseline and the review. The result can't be compared, and problems are found by everyone at once.

questions.prompt: What do the pilot numbers say about expanding now?

options.text: Expand: the draft is 25% faster, and speed is the goal of the project.
options.explanation: 6.0 to 4.5 days is 25% faster, but corrections rose too. The guide says to review quality and rework next to time.

options.text: Wait: the draft is 25% faster, but corrections rose from 9 to 15; find the cause.
options.explanation: Right. (6.0 - 4.5) / 6.0 = 25%. Corrections went up by 6, about two thirds. OpenAI's guide measures time and rework together, and reviews outcomes before expanding.

options.text: Expand: 15 corrections is a normal amount, because people always find errors in drafts.
options.explanation: The same people found 9 corrections before. The rise is the signal, and the cause is unknown.

options.text: Wait: the pilot is not valid, because eight people cannot be compared with themselves.
options.explanation: Comparing the same people before and after is the comparison the guide describes. The result is limited, not invalid.

questions.prompt: The senior accountant says the tool got a number wrong once. What is the best response?

options.text: Tell her the tool is improving every month, so she will have no problem next time.
options.explanation: Nothing in the guidance says to argue the general case, and a promise does not answer her concern.

options.text: Make the tool mandatory for her, so that she gains experience of it over time.
options.explanation: Forcing use adds pressure and no evidence. The champion kit suggests a demonstration, not an order.

options.text: Run her own report with the right data supplied, keeping her review step.
options.explanation: Right. The champion kit says to acknowledge the concern and offer one demonstration on the person's own work. It says wrong results are often a context problem.

options.text: Exclude her from the pilot, because doubts will slow the group down.
options.explanation: The kit says healthy skepticism is expected. Her reviews are useful evidence about errors.

questions.prompt: The CFO plans no review. What should the plan say about the time after launch?

options.text: No review is needed, because the pilot has already shown that the tool works well.
options.explanation: The pilot also showed more corrections. A review after launch is how that gets resolved.

options.text: A review after one year, so that enough data can be collected before anyone looks.
options.explanation: A year is too long to find friction. The guide ties the review to signals such as support feedback.

options.text: A review only if staff complain, because quiet means that everything works.
options.explanation: Silence is not a measure. Many problems show up in usage and rework, not in complaints.

options.text: A dated review of access, feedback, workflows used and usage; then adjust scope.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's rollout guide lists these items for the review after the initial rollout, and says to adjust scope and guidance.
